conviction_note: Nothing unpriced found: my arithmetic puts the Q3 property-management result about in line with the 176m Modular consensus. The September acquisitions closed on 30 Sep, 1 Oct and 15 Oct, so they add almost nothing to the quarter. They were all announced as inside information and analysts already model them. The release carries no guidance. So the findings sum to -0.2, and the scaled number is a slight negative lean (p_up 46: the company missed property-management consensus in Q3 2025 and Q2 2026, and 7 of its last 9 report days were down) on a 3.5% size.

already_public.what: Q2 2026 earnings capacity at 1 Jul 2026: NOI SEK 1,173m, property-management result SEK 678m, SEK 1.33/share. LTV 50.2%, ICR 2.6x, average interest rate 4.4%, hedge ratio 74.9%
Two fully let properties in Tampere and Oulu (SEK 145m) closed
Property in Norway divested to First Seafood AS
Velux portfolio in Denmark (inside information): SEK 1,010m, rent about SEK 78m, triple net, about 11-year leases, closing 15 Oct, financed with bank loans and own funds
DSV sale-leaseback in Stockholm (inside information): SEK 950m, rent SEK 72.5m triple net less SEK 5.8m leasehold fee, 7-year lease, closed 30 Sep, financed with bank loans and available funds
Helsinki property (SEK 142m) closed on 1 Oct, i.e. after the Q3 balance-sheet date
Modular Finance Q3 consensus from 6 estimates: rental income 329, NOI 306, property-management result SEK 176m

new_in_release.expect: Property-management result about SEK 172-178m against 176 consensus, i.e. in line to slightly below. NOI about 300-307 against 306. Q3 runs on the 1 July earnings capacity plus summer-low property costs, and the September deals add almost nothing to the quarter.

No formal guidance. Earnings capacity at 1 Oct should step up by about SEK 30m (about +4-5% per share) on the DSV deal, which closed 30 Sep, before Velux. The deals are public, so this is mechanical and mostly modelled.

LTV probably up from 50.2% toward about 51-53% at 30 Sep, and higher pro forma with Velux. Property value changes are unknown in sign as rates rise, with offsetting derivative gains. NRV/share moves either way from 17.78.
No change expected: SEK 0.20 for FY2025, paid quarterly.

findings.finding: None of the September/October acquisitions add to Q3: DSV closed 30 Sep, Helsinki 1 Oct, Velux 15 Oct, and only Tampere/Oulu (closed 20 Aug, SEK 145m) adds a few weeks of rent. So Q3 runs on the 1 July earnings capacity (NOI 1,173/4 = 293, property-management result 678/4 = 170) plus summer-low property costs (last year Q3 NOI ran about 13m above its run-rate). That gives about 172-178 against the 176 consensus. The company has missed property-management consensus in Q3 2025 (-6.5%) and Q2 2026 (-1.8%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: property-management result 1.8% under consensus, stock -2.9% on the day. Q3 2025: 6.5% under consensus, -1.0%. Q1 2026: +1.0%. Report-day moves over the last 9 prints were -2.9, +1.0, -2.8, -1.0, -0.5, -0.4, -1.3, -1.3, +7.2 (Modular table). Small moves with a downward skew.
findings.original_quote: Förvaltningsresultatet ökade till 165 miljoner kronor (131), vilket var 1,8 procent under konsensus från Modular Finance på 168 miljoner kronor. [Property-management result rose to SEK 165m (131), 1.8% below the Modular Finance consensus of SEK 168m] (https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/logistea-okar-forvaltningsresultatet-ungefar-i-linje-med-forvantningarna, 2026-07-09)
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is priced. The consensus of 176 already sits at the seasonal run-rate. If the market expected a September-deal contribution in Q3, consensus would sit near 185 rather than 176. The only unpriced edge is the company's habit of landing a few percent under, and that is an inference from two prints, not a document.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 miss on the same line: https://www.borsvarlden.com/artiklar/logisteas-forvaltningsresultat-kom-in-lagre-an-vantat-uppdatering-2

findings.finding: Earnings capacity at 1 Oct will step up because DSV closed on 30 Sep: NOI about SEK 66.7m (72.5 rent less 5.8 leasehold fee), debt-funded on about SEK 912m at about 4.4%, adds roughly +27-30m to the property-management result. With Tampere/Oulu and less the Norway sale, that is about +4-5% per share from 1.33. Velux (+78m rent) arrives in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earnings capacity is reported every quarter and has risen in each of the last 8 (0.94 to 1.33/share), and report-day moves stayed between -2.9% and +1.0% over the last 8 prints. A rising earnings capacity has not been rewarded on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. Both deals were released as inside information with rent and price. Pareto's 14 Oct note already models +31% property-management result per share for 2026, driven by acquisitions. The stock rose only 0.99% on the DSV day. If the market were missing it, sell-side estimates would not already embed it.

findings.finding: About SEK 2.1bn of September-October acquisitions are funded with 'bank loans and own funds/available funds' and no equity. Against SEK 9.4bn of debt on SEK 17.6bn of property at Q2 (LTV 50.2%), I infer LTV will print higher at 30 Sep and be about 53-55% pro forma with Velux, against a 60% cap. The company did directed share issues in March 2024 (SEK 250m) and June 2025 (SEK 500m), and the stock now trades at about 70% of SEK 17.78 NRV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed LTV up 1.8pp to 50.2% and the stock fell 2.9%, alongside a small miss. The 2025 equity issue came at a 3.1% discount (https://www.borskollen.se/pressmeddelanden/logistea-genomfor-en-riktad-nyemission-om-36-miljoner-b-aktier-och-tillfors-cirka-500-miljoner-kronor).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: both deals said how they were funded. The LTV figure itself is new in the release. What the money buys is 7.0-7.7% triple-net yields against a 4.4% average borrowing cost, which is accretive (see the earnings-capacity finding), so the sign is only a slight negative, from a balance-sheet and dilution-risk question in a rising-rate tape. If the market feared a placing, the stock would have fallen on the deal days, and it did not (+0.99% on 30 Sep).
findings.independence: Pareto and Arctic both cut targets while keeping buy, citing sector multiples rather than leverage: https://www.placera.se/telegram/logistea-arctic-securities-sanker-riktkursen-till-16-kr-19-20261001

baseline_tension: Agrees with the near-flat lean (+0.15) and the small negative 20-day run-up (-2.95%). The register gives no positioning anchor (truncated zero), and nothing found cuts strongly either way.
language_note: The Modular Finance Q3 consensus (rental income 329, NOI 306, property-management result 176, 6 estimates) and the report-day reaction table for the last 9 prints came only from Swedish Finwire copy on Börskollen/Placera. No English source carried a bar.
The Q2 2026 and Q3 2025 consensus misses (-1.8%, -6.5%) appear only in Swedish Finwire/Börsvärlden reports. The English release does not compare to consensus.
The Pareto (18 kr) and Arctic (16 kr) target cuts and Pareto's +31% 2026 per-share forecast were in Swedish wire copy only.
The FI insider register (Swedish) showed board buying in Jul-Aug and nothing since.
Company filings added nothing locally: every Logistea release is published in English and Swedish at once.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the earnings-capacity step-up rests on deals released as inside information, so it went from +0.2 to +0.1.
'Financing is a question': the money buys accretive 7.0-7.7% triple-net yields against 4.4% debt, with no placing, so the LTV finding went from -0.2 to -0.1.

'Too small about the move' / reaction history moves p_up, not abs_move: the numbers are new (not pre-released) but no guidance change is expected, so abs_move went from 3.0 to 3.5 rather than being held at this name's own about-1.3% median. p_up stays at 46.
The reported-quarter finding went from -0.3 to -0.2: it is an inference from the earnings-capacity arithmetic, and the bar comes from a single aggregator.
